tldr_label: TL;DR: A third US carrier reaches the Gulf as Iran escalates, Trump heads to Asia, and chip stocks slide before Nvidia reports

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: A third US carrier is reported to have arrived in the Middle East after Iran's second drone attack on Bahrain in three days. Iran claims a mined supertanker sank near Hormuz, which has not been independently verified. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

tldr_bullets.label: Asia trip
tldr_bullets.body: Trump leaves for Manila and Shenzhen, where a meeting with Xi and the first US-China-Russia leaders' trilateral are set for Thursday. [[TAG:info:Thursday]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: Asian chipmakers slumped before Nvidia's results on Tuesday. Japan's economy shrank for the first time in a year. [[TAG:warning:AI jitters]]

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: Estonia will close all crossings with Russia from December 1 after what it called a GRU-ordered sabotage attempt. The EU added 145 names to its Russia sanctions list. [[TAG:danger:border shut]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gaza
tldr_bullets.body: Israel killed Hamas's Rafah Brigade commander. Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urged Israel to allow rapid aid access. [[TAG:warning:ceasefire strain]]

sections.title: Gulf: Iran Escalates, US Reinforces
sections.summary: Third carrier arrives; GCC condemns Bahrain attack; Iran claims a sunken supertanker

paragraphs.heading: Bahrain
paragraphs.body: The National reported that Bahrain issued its first nationwide alert in months as it intercepted Iranian attacks aimed at a base hosting US helicopters. The National said Bahrain's defence force and foreign ministry gave different counts of the drones involved. It also reported that the GCC chief called the attack a 'blatant challenge' to peace efforts, and that Qatar, a mediator, called it a dangerous escalation. [[TAG:danger:GCC condemns]]

paragraphs.heading: Tanker Claims
paragraphs.body: Arab News reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers on an unauthorized route struck mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, and that one, a supertanker carrying over two million barrels, sank. There was no independent verification. A newsletter compiling the claims noted that UKMTO said it was aware of an Indian report of an attack on a Gulf tanker with the crew safe. [[TAG:warning:unverified]]

paragraphs.heading: Third Carrier
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and The National reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived, bringing the number of US carrier groups in the region to three, though the Pentagon had not formally confirmed it. Iran has stepped up threats against US forces and Gulf states. Reports said Trump is still talking with Iran through Qatari mediators. [[TAG:info:three carriers]]

paragraphs.heading: Houthis
paragraphs.body: The Tribune reported that the Houthis claimed missile strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport and financial center, and the Saudi-led coalition said both missiles were intercepted. The New Arab reported that Houthi attacks killed eight people in Yemen. [[TAG:danger:Riyadh targeted]]

sections.title: Trump's Asia Week
sections.summary: Manila first, then Shenzhen for Xi talks and the first US-China-Russia leaders' meeting

paragraphs.heading: Itinerary
paragraphs.body: ABC News reported that Trump will stop first in Manila for meetings with Southeast Asian leaders on Tuesday, then attend APEC in Shenzhen. On Thursday he holds a bilateral meeting and working lunch with Xi, followed by the first-ever trilateral with Xi and Putin. Trump and Putin are not scheduled to meet one-on-one. Newsweek said Trump and Xi are expected to discuss implementing their trade agreement. [[TAG:info:Thursday summit]]

paragraphs.heading: Backdrop
paragraphs.body: Deccan Chronicle said Trump travels after a midterm defeat and amid the Nvidia spy allegations. ABC News reported that a senior official said Trump is not expected to raise those allegations with Xi, or to raise Ukraine at the trilateral. The White House says he intends to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals. [[TAG:warning:Ukraine absent]]

sections.title: Markets: The AI Test Week
sections.summary: Asian chip stocks slide before Nvidia's Tuesday report; Japan's GDP shrinks

paragraphs.heading: Chip Sell-off
paragraphs.body: investingLive and Business Standard reported that Asian markets fell on Monday, led by chipmakers. Taiwan's benchmark dropped about 4.7%, and Korean chipmakers led regional losses. Business Standard said the AI rally faces tests this week from Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO. Reported Nikkei declines range from under 1% to about 2% depending on timing. Brent traded near $95. [[TAG:danger:chips slump]]

paragraphs.heading: Japan Contracts
paragraphs.body: Xinhua and the Seoul Economic Daily reported that Japan's real GDP shrank about 0.1% annualized in the third quarter, the first contraction in a year, against forecasts of modest growth. Private consumption fell 0.3% as higher prices weighed on households. [[TAG:warning:first drop in a year]]

paragraphs.heading: Nvidia and Anthropic
paragraphs.body: FXStreet and the Motley Fool said Nvidia's results on Tuesday will be its first since Jensen Huang's exit, with interim CEO Colette Kress leading the call against company guidance of about $108 billion in revenue. CNBC reported that Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 a share and expects to begin trading on November 19, according to sources. [[TAG:info:Tuesday earnings]]

sections.title: Europe: Borders and Sanctions
sections.summary: Estonia shuts Russia crossings after foiled GRU plot; EU lists 145 more; Canaries see record day

paragraphs.heading: Estonia
paragraphs.body: The Moscow Times and SCMP reported that Estonia will close all three border crossings with Russia, at Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa, from December 1. The government said it foiled a sabotage attempt ordered by Russian military intelligence: an attempted arson attack on the drone maker Threod Systems. Russia's foreign ministry called the move 'Russophobia.' Moscow denies orchestrating sabotage in Europe. [[TAG:danger:crossings close Dec 1]]

paragraphs.heading: Sanctions
paragraphs.body: APA and UNN reported that the EU added 145 individuals and entities to its Russia sanctions lists, targeting the financial system, the oil 'shadow fleet' and disinformation networks, according to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. Ministers said a 22nd sanctions package is being prepared. [[TAG:info:22nd package next]]

paragraphs.heading: Canary Islands
paragraphs.body: The Star, citing Reuters, and Spain in English reported that about 1,488 migrants reached the Canary Islands in one day, most of them landing on El Hierro, beating a 2020 record. Other outlets put the figure near 1,580. Arrivals through October were still down about 5.5% year on year. [[TAG:warning:record day]]

paragraphs.heading: Ukraine
paragraphs.body: NPR and the Kyiv Independent reported that the large prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi is expected within weeks. Zelensky has called it a positive step but says Ukraine will not cede occupied territory. [[TAG:info:swap pending]]

sections.title: Israel and Gaza
sections.summary: Yashar and Likud hold first formal talks; Israel kills Rafah Brigade chief; allies press on aid

paragraphs.heading: Unity Talks
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and the Jerusalem Post reported that negotiating teams from Eisenkot's Yashar and Netanyahu's Likud met on Sunday for coalition talks and issued a brief joint statement. Anadolu reported that beforehand Eisenkot called Netanyahu's unity appeal a 'media stunt.' Eisenkot maintains he will not serve in a Netanyahu-led government. Haaretz said Bennett's party also took part, a detail other outlets did not report. [[TAG:info:talks resume]]

paragraphs.heading: Rafah Commander
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Israel killed Samir Mahmoud Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, two months after killing his predecessor, as the ceasefire stagnates. Both Hamas and the Israeli military confirmed his death. [[TAG:danger:targeted killing]]

paragraphs.heading: Aid Appeal
paragraphs.body: SCMP reported that Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urged Israel to allow 'immediate, rapid and unimpeded' humanitarian access. They said 150,000 tents and other supplies were being held at the border. [[TAG:warning:aid blocked]]

sections.title: Pope in the Amazon
sections.summary: In Pucallpa, Leo demands justice for slain environmental defenders and condemns abuses

paragraphs.heading: Pucallpa
paragraphs.body: AP, via Audacy, and Al Jazeera reported that Pope Leo XIV, speaking in the Peruvian Amazon city of Pucallpa, demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the forest. He backed Indigenous efforts against illegal logging and mining. Vatican News said he decried human rights abuses and exploitation and invoked Pope Francis's 2018 Amazon visit. Counts of slain defenders vary by source and time frame. [[TAG:warning:impunity]]
